summary: This investigative piece examines how cyber attacks threaten internet reliability and how cybersecurity keeps networks running. It cites dated outages and attacks from 2023-2024, expert views on firewalls, layered defenses and AI, and the role of legislation and international cooperation. It concludes that continual adaptation, education, information sharing and security-by-design are needed to stay ahead of cybercriminals.
one_line: An investigative piece on how DDoS, phishing and AI-driven cyber threats disrupt the internet, and how defenses, laws and collaboration preserve its continuity.
key_facts: On October 15, 2023, a major service provider suffered a wide-scale outage that affected thousands of users across the East Coast.
On November 3, 2023, another wave of outages swept the Midwest, affecting countless businesses and individuals.
On September 5, 2023, a coordinated DDoS attack crippled the servers of a prominent online retailer for hours, causing significant revenue loss.
Dr. Emily Chen likened a DDoS attack to "an orchestrated siege" in which cybercriminals use botnets to generate an overwhelming amount of fake traffic.
Security analyst Marcus Reynolds said a properly configured firewall can block up to 90% of incoming threats, but firewalls are not impregnable and rules must be continuously updated.
On December 9, 2023, a sophisticated email phishing campaign targeted employees of multiple financial institutions; a vigilant employee prevented a potential breach despite the advanced firewalls.
Aaron Zhang, CISO of TechAdvance, said the company uses machine learning algorithms to detect anomalies in network behavior and block threats before they reach critical systems.
On January 23, 2024, an AI-driven security system foiled an attempt to breach a government database in real time.
Cybersecurity consultant Jaime Patterson warned that hackers can use AI to automate the creation and variation of malware and to conduct intelligent phishing schemes mimicking trusted sources.

The U.S. Congress passed the Internet Security Act of 2024, mandating stricter cybersecurity standards for critical sectors; Senator Elizabeth Harper supports it as a vital step toward a more resilient internet.
The Global Cyber Alliance, initiated on February 11, 2024, brings together experts and stakeholders from various countries to combat cyber threats through unified action.
The article advocates 'building security in' rather than 'adding it on', and points to blockchain and DNS over HTTPS (DoH) as forward-thinking approaches.
